answer.summary: No existing evidence supports implicit temporal memory or state continuity in agent systems under stable input conditions without predefined features or feature vectors.
answer.content: The repeated absence of explicit, non-feature-based mechanisms for temporal smoothing, sequence coherence, or state persistence in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 confirms a gap in documented memory dynamics under low-variation input. The inquiry must now shift to whether any agent system reports latent state inference through patterned behavioral drift rather than explicit modeling of continuity metrics or feature vectors.
answer.search: handoff to analyst to retrieve and inspect Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 for explicit descriptions of latent behavioral drift or patterned response shifts in agent memory under stable, low-variation input conditions without predefined feature vectors; if any

answer.lesson: Temporal memory claims without observable, non-feature-based indicators must be anchored to explicit behavioral or metric-level evidence before being considered valid proxy signals for continuity or persistence in agent systems.
